name: Rob Jetten
role: Prime Minister of the Netherlands (minister-president) and Minister of General Affairs
bio: Rob Jetten, born in Veghel in 1987 and a public-administration graduate of Radboud University Nijmegen, has been Prime Minister of the Netherlands and Minister of General Affairs since 23 February 2026: the youngest holder of the office, the first from D66 and the first who is openly gay. After chairing the Young Democrats, sitting on Nijmegen city council (2010–2017) and working for rail-infrastructure manager ProRail, he entered the House of Representatives in 2017, became D66 parliamentary leader at 31 in 2018 and was Minister for Climate and Energy Policy in the fourth Rutte cabinet (2022–2024), also serving as Deputy Prime Minister in the first half of 2024. D66 leader since August 2023, he took the party from 9 seats in 2023 to 26 in the October 2025 election, its best result, finishing first by 29,668 votes ahead of the PVV. After a four-month formation he heads a D66–VVD–CDA minority cabinet holding 66 of the 150 seats in the House and 22 of 75 in the Senate, which has to find majorities with opposition parties for each proposal. As of October 2026 his government had dropped the coalition agreement's faster rise in the state pension age and its unemployment- and disability-benefit cuts in order to restart talks with unions and employers, presented a €20 billion nitrogen package, and was still seeking parliamentary majorities for its first budget and tax plan for 2027.
